chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Murram, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The deceased has more right to his wealth as long as the soul is in him, he can clarify/disperse it with it; and if he says 'after me', it is not for him [to give all] except one-third."
ai.seo_question: What is the limit of a dying person's bequest according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of the 'dying person' (marid) by linking the right of full disposal to the presence of the soul, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the transition from life to death. It establishes that while the individual retains complete authority over their wealth as long as the soul has not fully departed, any formal bequest (wasiyyah) made is strictly capped at one-third of the total estate, preserving the rights of heirs.
